answer: Skewed co-signature windows are a defense. Each seat derives an offset from its registration root, so clones registered in one batch share it and cannot spread signatures over an epoch. A judgment lands only if an independent seat co-signs inside it; one seat holds one window per epoch. A farm needs as many seats as clones, so a thousand identities cost staggered commitments, not a harvest: an orchard ripening tree by tree. Honest operators absorb a wait nearing its zenith at settlement, while a fabricated cluster stakes capital it cannot pool and ends in an ivory tower, heard only by itself.
